instructions: Up to 3 months ahead: whisk the 12 eggs, 2 tbsp water, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper in a large bowl until they're a little frothy.
Heat the 2 tsp olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the spinach and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until it's all wilted. Transfer it to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium low and pour the eggs into the same skillet. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring gently, until they're set but still soft. Take the pan off the heat.
Fold the spinach and the 1/2 cup feta into the eggs. Let the filling cool for about 10 minutes.
Drain the roasted red peppers and slice them into strips.
Spread a spoonful of the sun-dried tomato pesto over the middle of each tortilla.
Divide the filling between the tortillas and lay a few pepper strips on each.
Fold in the sides and roll each one up tightly. This makes 8 wraps.
Let them cool completely. Wrap each one in foil and put them in a freezer bag.

They keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months. The night before, move one to the fridge to thaw. In the morning, take off the foil and microwave it for about 1 minute, until it's hot through.
advance_prep_notes: Make and wrap the wraps up to 3 months ahead for the freezer.
method_notes: None of the wraps read had 20 or more ratings, so this follows fANNEtastic Food, the first one read and the closest to a freezer batch. All three roll eggs, spinach and feta in a tortilla with something tomato. fANNEtastic scrambles 12 whole eggs, folds in wilted spinach and feta and spreads sun-dried tomato pesto inside with roasted red peppers; The Girl on Bloor copies the coffee shop wrap with an egg white omelet and a sun-dried tomato cream cheese, and An Oregon Cottage uses tomato chutney and crisps the wraps in a pan. The lead's 8 wraps are kept as written.
